title: Bandits with increasing mean trajectories and a known variation budget
summary: All arms evolve in calendar time, including unselected arms. Their fixed unknown means increase, without a concavity requirement. The learner observes only the selected arm's fresh reward and compares with the largest current mean; the variation budget is known.

model.instance: Reward laws $\nu_i(t)$ for the $K\ge2$ arms are fixed before interaction and evolve with absolute time, including for unpulled arms. Means satisfy $$\mu_i(t)=\mathbb E_{X\sim\nu_i(t)}X\in[0,1],\qquad \gamma_i(t)=\mu_i(t+1)-\mu_i(t)\ge0.$$. Decreasing increments are not required; there is no temporal concavity assumption. $$V_\mu=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\max_{i\in[K]}\gamma_i(t)\le V,\qquad 0\le V\le K.$$

operations.query_signature: Choose $I_t\in[K]$ from past observations and receive only $X_{I_t,t}$. Each $X_{i,t}$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian around $\mu_i(t)$ and independent of the reward table before round $t$; within-round dependence across arms is permitted. bounds.derivation: Divide rewards by $2\sigma$, yielding the source sub-Gaussian parameter $1/2$ and variation $V/(2\sigma)$. With restart length $h$, the original-scale upper bound is $O(Vh+\sigma T\sqrt{K/h}+\sigma\sqrt{Kh})$. Restrict $h$ to $[1,T]$ and balance the terms; if $V=0$, choose $h=T$. Mean gaps per round are at most one, giving the additional cap $T$. The algorithm needs no monotonicity and therefore applies to the increasing subclass.
